name: NPC Conversion Advisor for WooCommerce
author: NPCoding LTD

sections.description:
Most conversion advice is generic. This plugin looks at your own store and tells you where it is losing buyers, what to change, and what that change is worth — as a range, with the assumption written next to it.

What it looks at

  • Your funnel: product views, add to cart, cart, checkout and orders, on phones and on computers.
  • Popular products that people view but cannot buy (for example, the most wanted size is sold out).
  • Your free-shipping threshold: orders that land just under it, and whether every page shows the same number.
  • Where shoppers leave, step by step.
  • Your store’s own pages, every night: the home page, the cart, the shipping and returns page, your most viewed product and category pages, and one more product and category page that change every day, so over the weeks every page is checked. On each: is there a delivery and returns line by the buy button, do reviews show, how many photos does the product have, and how much the page weighs (what your theme, plugins and tags add – WordPress’s and WooCommerce’s own files are not counted). And can a shopper see what shipping costs before the checkout: does any product page checked name a shipping cost by the buy button, and does your cart show shipping before an address is typed (it does not when “Hide shipping costs until an address is entered” is on, or with no default customer location).
  • Your checkout settings: guest checkout, how many fields buyers fill in, and quick payment options (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal). When the plugin does not know your payment plugin, it says nothing about quick payment rather than guess.

A full store audit from the first day

Within a minute of switching the plugin on, before a single visit is counted, it audits your store and shows the result on its page; with the daily email on, it comes by email at once. Then a fresh audit every morning of the first week, and whenever you press “Scan my store now”. The audit reads:

  • About ten pages of your store: delivery and returns by the buy button, reviews, photos, and speed (how long the server takes, how much the page weighs, the biggest photo, scripts that hold up the page).
  • Your whole catalog (up to 5,000 products): products with no photo, only one photo, no price, a very short description, or sold out and still shown.
  • Your orders of the last 30 days: orders just under the free-shipping threshold, payment success by system, and orders left unpaid.
  • Your checkout settings and trust: guest checkout, the fields asked for, quick payments, a way to reach you, the returns page, a secure address.
  • The tracking: tags set up twice on a page, and whether the advisor’s own counts get through (some security plugins and hosts block them).

Each finding comes with what to do and how. Money is shown only where your own orders give it, as a range with its assumption; a finding without that is shown with what was found, never with a made-up sum.

Your dashboard from the first day

As soon as the plugin is on, its page opens with your store’s last 30 days, read from your WooCommerce orders (so also the days before you installed it): sales, paid orders, the average order, orders that were not paid and what they were worth, product views, and the fixes waiting. Below them, sales by day and product views by day (point at a day for its numbers, or open the table), your best sellers, and where your orders come from (search, social media, ads, email, direct). The figures are refreshed every day.

At the top of the dashboard, “Your store’s flow” draws the path from product view to paid order: product views, added to cart, reached checkout and orders, each with its count and the share that went on, and how many left between two steps. The step to fix is marked with the reason, what was found in your numbers, and the one-click change for it, with the orders and money a month it should add and how that was counted. Its button opens the same simulation as the change below, with Apply there. Once a change is on, its step shows that it is being measured. With too few counts, or no checkout view counted, the flow says so and marks no step. The daily email shows the same flow, and its button opens the dashboard: nothing changes from the email.

A small box on the WordPress dashboard shows the sales, the paid orders and the fixes waiting, with a button to the full page; hide it in Screen Options if you do not want it. After activation a welcome box on the Plugins screen takes you to the page, and the plugin’s row in the Plugins list has a “Dashboard” link.

What it gives you

  • One to three changes a day, ranked by the money at stake in your store.
  • For each: what was found (in your numbers), why it matters, what to do, what it may be worth, and how the result will be measured.
  • Every estimate is a range with its assumption, never a promise.

Privacy

The plugin counts page views and add-to-carts as daily totals on your own site, by device class (phone or computer) and product. It stores nothing personal, sets no cookie, and sends nothing to any other site unless you connect it to NPCoding (see External services). Visits by robots and by the shop’s own staff are not counted. Counts older than 90 days are deleted every day.

To find where buyers leave, it reads your WooCommerce orders in place (totals, products, the device type and the source WooCommerce records with each order) and works only with totals: no customer’s name, email, address or IP address is used or copied.

Every night the plugin also asks your own site for about ten of its pages, as a shopper who is not signed in sees them, one a second, each with a time limit, so a page that does not answer never holds up the report. It never asks another site and never follows a redirect to one. It keeps only what its checks need – the product’s own area as bare markup (no text, so no reviewer’s name or words), the text by the buy button, the number of photos and scripts, the page’s size – and replaces it the next night. These requests run no script, so they are not counted as visits. In WooCommerce’s “coming soon” mode nothing is asked.

The store audit reads your published products in place (the name, how long the description is, whether there is a photo, a price and stock) and keeps only the names of the products a finding is about. To see whether its counts get through, it asks your own site’s counting address once, marked as a test, so nothing is counted.

The diagnosis appears after seven whole days of counting.

Your page (Conversion Advisor, in the admin menu)

  • The dashboard of your last 30 days (above).
  • Where your store stands, from product view to order.
  • What today’s changes could add together: orders, percentage and money a month, as a range, with no buyer counted twice.
  • Today’s one to three changes, each with numbered steps, what to do and what not to do, and two buttons: “I made this change” and “Not for my store”. A change is never shown as new twice; one you have not answered stays under “Still open”.
  • Being measured: after you mark a change as made, orders per 100 product views in the days after it against the 14 days before it. The verdict (helped, did not help, or not clear) comes once, when the 14 days are over, because a difference read every day looks like more than chance far too often. From the first day it says how large a rise those 14 days can show at your store’s numbers, so a small gain that does not show is not read as a failure.
  • Growth so far: only measured results, never estimates.

The page’s fonts and logo are part of the plugin; the page loads nothing from another site. The page mirrors itself when WordPress runs right to left.

Pro (optional, paid)

Everything above is free and works fully without Pro. The Pro add-on, NPC Conversion Advisor Pro, makes the changes for you: “Do it for me” on the changes the advisor can make itself (a free-shipping progress bar, a sticky buy bar on phones, a delivery date line on products, a back-in-stock sign-up), each after your own click and with undo at any time, “Do it now” in the daily email, and a verdict 14 days after each change.

It is priced by your store’s paid orders a month: $39 (up to 100), $69 (up to 300), $119 (up to 1,000), $199 (up to 3,000) or $349 (more), or yearly for the price of ten months. “Do it now” on the advisor’s page and in the email opens the secure checkout, run by Freemius, NPCoding’s seller, on the plan that fits your store’s paid orders of the last 30 days; you can cancel any time. The licence key and the Pro download come by email.

The daily email (on from the start)

Every morning, from the first day:

  • In the first week: a fresh store audit – what each area checked, the three things to fix first with their steps, and the rest – and yesterday’s counts (product views, add to cart, cart and checkout views, on phones and on computers). Money only where your own orders give it; the money from the counts comes with the first diagnosis.
  • Then: today’s cards – the same cards as on your page, with the steps, what each may be worth as a range, and a link to the card on your page, where you mark it as made or not for your store.
  • On a day without new cards: a short note of what is still open and what is being measured.

It is sent at most once a day, early in the morning by your store’s clock, by your own site with WordPress’s mail (wp_mail), only to the addresses you choose (up to five; by default the site’s admin email). Switch it on, off or change the addresses in “Daily email” on the page.

Scan my store now

The button under the email’s settings makes a fresh whole-store audit on every press and emails it at once, even before the first diagnosis. It takes up to about a minute; a second press within a minute is ignored, so a double click sends once. Every day the plugin also prepares the report in the night, so the page opens at once.

External services

This plugin can connect to one external service, NPCoding’s (NPCoding makes this plugin), and only after a shop manager agrees. It is off until a shop manager presses “Connect” in the plugin’s notice or switches on “Connected to NPCoding” on the Conversion Advisor page; nothing is sent before that.

What it is for: so NPCoding can see that your store’s reports work and help you with them.

When it is sent: once when you connect, then once a day (with the plugin’s daily job) while you stay connected, and once when you disconnect. After the disconnect nothing more is sent.

What is sent: the site’s address and name, the site’s admin email, the WooCommerce and plugin versions, the store’s currency, country and time zone, the day the plugin was switched on, the report’s totals for the last 30 days (days counted, product page views, paid orders, sales, conversion rate, average order, currency), and for the last 5 report emails their day, subject, whether it was sent and how many addresses it went to (not the addresses). No shopper’s data is sent.

Where it is sent: https://europe-west1-npcoding-dashboard.cloudfunctions.net/cro_connect (a Google Cloud Functions address run by NPCoding).

The Pro “Do it now” buttons are plain links to the checkout page of Freemius (https://freemius.com), which sells the Pro add-on for NPCoding; the plugin sends nothing to Freemius, and the page opens only when you press one. Freemius’ terms: https://freemius.com/terms/ and privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

NPCoding’s privacy policy: https://npcoding.ca/privacy-policy/
NPCoding’s terms of use: https://npcoding.ca/terms-of-use/

Credits

The page uses the Rubik and Assistant fonts, both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (licence texts in assets/fonts).

WooCommerce is a trademark of Automattic Inc.; WordPress is a trademark of the WordPress Foundation; Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal are trademarks of their owners. This plugin is an add-on for WooCommerce, made independently: it is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.
sections.installation:
1. Make sure WooCommerce (7.0 or later) is installed and active.
  2. Install this plugin from Plugins > Add New Plugin (or upload its folder to /wp-content/plugins/) and activate it.
  3. Press “Open my dashboard” in the welcome box, or “Dashboard” on the plugin’s row, or open Conversion Advisor in the admin menu. Your last 30 days and the store audit are there within a minute; counting starts at once; the first diagnosis appears after seven whole days.
  4. The daily email is on from the start, to the addresses under “Daily email” on that page, where you can also switch it off. “Scan my store now” there emails a fresh store audit at once. Every email has a “Stop these emails” link.
sections.faq:
Does it slow down my store?

It adds one small counter per page view on product, cart and checkout pages, sent after the page has loaded. Once a night it asks your site for about ten pages, one a second, and stops after 20 seconds at most.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The count is sent by a small script after the page loads, so cached pages are counted too, as long as the cache is refreshed at least once a day (the counter carries a security token that WordPress renews daily).

Are the estimates guaranteed?

No. Every figure is an estimate, not a promise or a guarantee. It comes from your store’s own numbers and published benchmarks, and real results depend on many things the plugin cannot control: your traffic and where it comes from, the season, prices and competitors, stock, advertising, and how each change is made. Each change is measured after it goes live, so you see what really happened.

Do I have to pay?

No. The dashboard, the store audit, the daily changes, the measurements and the daily email are free, with no time limit. Pro is an optional add-on that makes the changes for you; see “Pro (optional, paid)” above.

Does it send my data anywhere?

Not unless you connect it. Everything stays in your WordPress database. The nightly check of your pages is your site asking itself for its own pages. The daily email leaves your site unless you switch it off: your own site sends it, through its own mail setup, to the address you chose. If you press “Connect” (it is off until you do), a short daily record of your store goes to NPCoding, the makers of the plugin; see External services for what it holds. You can disconnect at any time on the Conversion Advisor page.
sections.changelog:
0.5.2

  • New “Your store’s flow” at the top of the dashboard: product views, added to cart, reached checkout and orders, each with its count and the share that went on, and how many left between the steps. Every step that is worse than a benchmark this plugin cites is marked, with the reason, the comparison and its source link, and the one-click change or what to check. The biggest keeps “Most shoppers leave here”.
  • The daily email and the store audit email open with the fixes (title, the gain in green, its own “See the effect and apply” button) before the flow. “Each fix in full” and the repeated traffic block are gone, so the email is far shorter on phones.
  • A fix whose own counts give no number shows no figure and no money and counts in no total.
  • The “Likely figure. Range …” line is no longer repeated under the buttons when the card already shows its range.
  • One source and one 30-day window for the order count, everywhere.
  • Conversion first and large (“conversion 1.90% -> 2.06%”, “+8.7% more buyers”), the money underneath, smaller, labelled “estimate”. The same order on the flow’s fix card and in the decisions list.
  • “Do it now” buys Pro, in the emails and on the dashboard, only on changes that Pro makes and this free plugin does not, with “The change is made with Pro, from $X a month” under it ($X is the plan that fits your last 30 days of paid orders). One-click changes in this plugin stay free.
  • The email of a day without new changes never reads as empty: it opens with the one thing to do (the open change worth the most, else the step furthest below the benchmark this plugin cites, else the change being measured and the day its result is ready), with one button to the exact place. Each number shows its change against the week before (arrow and %), the benchmark and one line of what it means.
  • If half or more of the pages did not answer in time, the page check is repeated once the same morning before anything is mailed; if it fails again the email says plainly that the site answered slowly, that the pages could not be checked, and when it tries again.
  • The email follows the site’s language: right to left with the date in that language. A Hebrew translation of the email is bundled in languages/.
  • Benchmarks and published figures are shown as “the average store” and “published industry benchmarks” instead of the name of the company that published them; the numbers are the same.

0.5.1

  • New dashboard at the top of the advisor’s page, from the first day: sales, paid orders, the average order, orders not paid, product views and the fixes waiting for the last 30 days (read from your WooCommerce orders, so also the days before you installed the plugin), sales by day and product views by day with each day’s numbers on hover and as a table, your best sellers and where your orders come from. Refreshed every day.
  • The dashboard opens with “What your numbers show”: the 2 or 3 findings worth the most, first those found in your own orders (buyers who tried to pay and did not, orders just under free shipping, payments failing on one kind of phone, products bought together). Each one shows what fixing it should be worth and how to fix it: the steps, or with Pro a “Do it for me” button.
  • The advisor has its own item in the admin menu, “Conversion Advisor”, instead of a submenu under WooCommerce.
  • After activation a welcome box on the Plugins screen and the WordPress dashboard: the audit’s state and an “Open my dashboard” button, until you open the page or press “Not now”. The plugin’s row has a “Dashboard” link.
  • A box on the WordPress dashboard with the sales, paid orders and fixes waiting, and a button to the full page (hide it in Screen Options).
  • The Pro card always has its buy button, with the price for your store’s size written under it.
  • The “Connect to NPCoding” question is asked on the advisor’s page only, no longer on the Plugins screen.

0.5.0

  • Every change shows its expected gain from day 1: “+X% orders (about N orders and an amount a month)”. The number is your own last 30 days of WooCommerce orders times a published range, with the source, the figure it quotes and the assumption written beside it, and it says it is an estimate until measured. After a week of your own counts the number switches to your store’s own and says so. With no orders yet only the percentage range shows, never an invented amount. Changes with no specific study use a general range and are labelled that way.
  • A button on each change opens a simulation without leaving the page: now against with the change (orders and money a month, counted up unless you ask for reduced motion), a preview on one of your products, the basis, how it will be measured (14 days after against 14 days before), and Apply or Not now. The buttons in the daily email open the same simulation.
  • New “What to do with your traffic” section in the page and the daily email: the drop-offs from product to cart, cart to checkout and checkout to order against published benchmarks, and the visit sources (search, social, ads, email, direct, other) with the source that converts best and one action for each.
  • Visit sources are counted as one number per day and source group. No cookie, no IP address, no referrer address and nothing personal is stored, and nothing leaves your site.

0.4.5

  • In the first week the REST status shows the store audit’s fixes, the same ones the email shows, instead of none.

0.4.4

  • REST status gives the dashboard the full picture: funnel, weeks, best sellers, every open fix with its money, fix history, next run.

0.4.3

  • Two REST routes for a shop manager (an application password works): GET npcca/v1/status gives the site’s record (its name, address and settings, the day the plugin was switched on, who gets the email, the numbers of the counted days, the last emails and the last scan), and POST npcca/v1/report makes the “Scan my store now” report and returns it without sending it, once a minute at most.
  • The plugin keeps its last 10 emails (when, which, to whom, sent or not, the subject); deleting the plugin removes them.
  • A store with few visits gets no money a month: with no paid order yet, or when all the fixes together add under one sale a month, the email and the page say how often a sale is likely to come (“about 1 more sale every 7 months”), and that more visitors come first.
  • “Connect to NPCoding”, off until you say yes: a one-time notice (Connect or No thanks) and a switch on the Conversion Advisor page. Once connected, a short record of the store goes to NPCoding on connect, once a day, and once on disconnect. See External services.

0.4.2

  • The daily email opens with its conclusions in figures: the rise of the conversion rate (and of the order size when a fix moves it), the extra orders and the extra sales a month, each with its range, and one line on what the figures rest on.
  • Every fix shows what it adds right before its buttons, in the summary and in the fix in full: conversion +X% (or order size +X% for a fix that makes orders bigger, like the free-delivery line) and the money a month, with the range under it.
  • More fixes are put into numbers: the buy bar on phones from your phone orders, hiding sold-out products from the views of the products that are sold out now, and the shorter checkout from the boxes of your own checkout form. A fix that cannot be put into numbers says why in one line.
  • A store with fewer than 10 paid orders gets an estimate too: its own product views a month at the average store’s conversion and its average order (or the average price of its most viewed products), said in one line.
  • Every fix says how it raises the conversion, right under its title: what its button changes on your store, what the shopper then does, and the step and the conversion it moves, from your own numbers (for example: of those who reach checkout, pay 39.2% → 39.3%, so your conversion 2.91% → 2.92%). The headline, the conversion box and the figure by each fix’s buttons show the rate itself (conversion 2.91% → 3.19%), so a rise is never read as percentage points; the ranges count more buyers.
  • In a right-to-left language, a sentence that is not translated yet keeps its full stop at its end.

0.4.1

  • The daily email opens with “Your decisions today”: every fix in one line with its effect and its buttons together (Apply on my store, or Open on your page, and “I made this” / “Not for us”), above the fixes in full.
  • “I made this” and “Not for us” work from the email without logging in: the link opens a page with one button, and only that button records the answer, so a mail scanner that opens links answers nothing.

0.4.0

  • The daily email now opens with the combined effect in percent (“These 5 fixes: about +14% more orders”) and shows every fix in full: what happens on your store when you click, what it is based on (your own numbers and a named study), and the effect (conversion rate from X% to Y%, orders and sales a month).
  • One-click changes: free-delivery line in the cart, delivery cost on product pages, a buy bar on phones, a trust line from your real payment methods and returns page, guest checkout, hiding sold-out products, a shorter checkout. The email button opens the plugin’s page; Apply there needs a signed-in shop manager, and Undo puts everything back.
  • A fix that cannot be put into numbers honestly says so.

0.3.1

  • The daily email is on from activation (a store that saved it off keeps it off). The full store audit comes by email a minute after activation, then every morning.
  • Every email has a “Stop these emails” link that works without logging in.
  • “Check my pages now” is now “Scan my store now”: every press makes a fresh scan and emails it at once (no daily limit, a 60-second guard against a double click).
  • The settings and scan forms send their security token under a name of their own, because some hosts refuse a POST with _wpnonce.

0.3.0

  • A full store audit from the first day: about ten pages, the whole catalog, the last 30 days of orders, the checkout settings, trust and tracking, with what to fix first. On the page within a minute of switching the plugin on, by email at once when the daily email is switched on, every morning of the first week, and with “Scan my store now”.
  • New checks: products with no photo, one photo only, no price, a very short description, or sold out and still shown; unpaid orders; server time, the biggest photo and scripts that hold up a page; a way to reach you; tags set up twice; whether the advisor’s own counts get through.
  • The email and the page never show a bare row of zeros: a count of none is said in words.
  • The visit counter no longer depends on WordPress’s REST nonce, which caching plugins can serve stale and some hosts refuse: it sends a token of its own that changes every week.
  • The lists in the email are joined in the email’s own language (a Hebrew “and” appeared in English emails on Hebrew sites).

0.2.0

  • The daily email comes every morning from the first day: in the first week yesterday’s counts and what the look at your pages found; on a day without new cards, a short note of what is still open and what is being measured.
  • “Check my pages now”: a check of the main pages at once, by email, once a day.
  • The daily email can go to up to five addresses.

0.1.0

  • First version: collects daily counts (product, cart and checkout views, add to cart) by device class; the daily diagnosis page with today’s changes, what is still open, what is being measured and what was measured. The daily email and the nightly report. The nightly check of the store’s own pages and checkout settings.

Your page (Conversion Advisor, in the admin menu)

  • The dashboard of your last 30 days (above).
  • Where your store stands, from product view to order.
  • What today’s changes could add together: orders, percentage and money a month, as a range, with no buyer counted twice.
  • Today’s one to three changes, each with numbered steps, what to do and what not to do, and two buttons: “I made this change” and “Not for my store”. A change is never shown as new twice; one you have not answered stays under “Still open”.
  • Being measured: after you mark a change as made, orders per 100 product views in the days after it against the 14 days before it. The verdict (helped, did not help, or not clear) comes once, when the 14 days are over, because a difference read every day looks like more than chance far too often. From the first day it says how large a rise those 14 days can show at your store’s numbers, so a small gain that does not show is not read as a failure.
  • Growth so far: only measured results, never estimates.

The page’s fonts and logo are part of the plugin; the page loads nothing from another site. The page mirrors itself when WordPress runs right to left.

Pro (optional, paid)

Everything above is free and works fully without Pro. The Pro add-on, NPC Conversion Advisor Pro, makes the changes for you: “Do it for me” on the changes the advisor can make itself (a free-shipping progress bar, a sticky buy bar on phones, a delivery date line on products, a back-in-stock sign-up), each after your own click and with undo at any time, “Do it now” in the daily email, and a verdict 14 days after each change.

It is priced by your store’s paid orders a month: $39 (up to 100), $69 (up to 300), $119 (up to 1,000), $199 (up to 3,000) or $349 (more), or yearly for the price of ten months. “Do it now” on the advisor’s page and in the email opens the secure checkout, run by Freemius, NPCoding’s seller, on the plan that fits your store’s paid orders of the last 30 days; you can cancel any time. The licence key and the Pro download come by email.

The daily email (on from the start)

Every morning, from the first day:

  • In the first week: a fresh store audit – what each area checked, the three things to fix first with their steps, and the rest – and yesterday’s counts (product views, add to cart, cart and checkout views, on phones and on computers). Money only where your own orders give it; the money from the counts comes with the first diagnosis.
  • Then: today’s cards – the same cards as on your page, with the steps, what each may be worth as a range, and a link to the card on your page, where you mark it as made or not for your store.
  • On a day without new cards: a short note of what is still open and what is being measured.

It is sent at most once a day, early in the morning by your store’s clock, by your own site with WordPress’s mail (wp_mail), only to the addresses you choose (up to five; by default the site’s admin email). Switch it on, off or change the addresses in “Daily email” on the page.

Scan my store now

The button under the email’s settings makes a fresh whole-store audit on every press and emails it at once, even before the first diagnosis. It takes up to about a minute; a second press within a minute is ignored, so a double click sends once. Every day the plugin also prepares the report in the night, so the page opens at once.

External services

This plugin can connect to one external service, NPCoding’s (NPCoding makes this plugin), and only after a shop manager agrees. It is off until a shop manager presses “Connect” in the plugin’s notice or switches on “Connected to NPCoding” on the Conversion Advisor page; nothing is sent before that.

What it is for: so NPCoding can see that your store’s reports work and help you with them.

When it is sent: once when you connect, then once a day (with the plugin’s daily job) while you stay connected, and once when you disconnect. After the disconnect nothing more is sent.

What is sent: the site’s address and name, the site’s admin email, the WooCommerce and plugin versions, the store’s currency, country and time zone, the day the plugin was switched on, the report’s totals for the last 30 days (days counted, product page views, paid orders, sales, conversion rate, average order, currency), and for the last 5 report emails their day, subject, whether it was sent and how many addresses it went to (not the addresses). No shopper’s data is sent.

Where it is sent: https://europe-west1-npcoding-dashboard.cloudfunctions.net/cro_connect (a Google Cloud Functions address run by NPCoding).

The Pro “Do it now” buttons are plain links to the checkout page of Freemius (https://freemius.com), which sells the Pro add-on for NPCoding; the plugin sends nothing to Freemius, and the page opens only when you press one.
